subject.title: refactor(plugin-sdk): isolate core session state from plugin mutations

question: Should the shipped `getAcpSessionManager()` class-identity contract be preserved while its public outputs are hardened, or may this PR intentionally break that contract immediately to close the isolation escape?
rationale: Repository policy favors staged Plugin SDK compatibility, while the contributor argues that preserving constructor and prototype identity reopens the private-session-state boundary; choosing the permanent public contract requires explicit owner intent.

options.title: Preserve identity, harden outputs
options.body: Keep the existing getter identity and move projection into its plugin-visible methods or another internal/public split so private recovery state is inaccessible without breaking current callers.

options.title: Approve immediate security break
options.body: Accept the facade replacement now with explicit owner approval, migration guidance, release communication, and compatibility tests documenting the intentionally unsupported identity behavior.

options.title: Defer removal to breaking release
options.body: Introduce the facade API additively now and remove concrete manager identity only in the next approved breaking Plugin SDK release.

recommendation.title: Preserve identity, harden outputs
recommendation.body: Keep the existing getter identity and move projection into its plugin-visible methods or another internal/public split so private recovery state is inaccessible without breaking current callers.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice sets the permanent shipped Plugin SDK compatibility and security-boundary contract.
